info.name: FreightID — Jumio Auth & Workflow Retrieval
info.description:
Two requests against Jumio's live API: obtain a bearer token, then read back a workflow execution result.

These are steps 1 and 4 of the flow in docs/Jumio_SDK_API_Flow.md. Steps 2 and 3 (create account, upload, finalize) are not included — this collection is for inspecting a workflow the app has already started.

Hosts default to the amer-1 datacenter, matching JUMIO_DATACENTER in .env. Each is a separate hostname: auth, account and retrieval are not interchangeable.

Setup:
1. Collection → Variables → set `clientId` and `clientSecret` from JUMIO_CLIENT_ID / JUMIO_CLIENT_SECRET. Set **Current value**, not Initial value, so the secret is not synced to Postman's cloud.
2. Run "Step 1". The test script stores `accessToken` for you.
3. Set `accountId` and `workflowExecutionId` — they are the `jumio_account_id` and `jumio_workflow_id` columns on `driver_verifications` / `document_checks`.
4. Run "Step 4".

request.description:
OAuth 2.0 client-credentials grant — mirrors src/lib/jumio/auth.ts.

Basic auth appears here and only here, to obtain the bearer token. Every API call afterwards is Bearer; this is not the legacy Basic-auth API integration.

The token is valid for 3600s and this endpoint is rate limited to 10 requests/second, so reuse the token rather than re-requesting it per call. The app caches it in memory and refreshes 120s before expiry.

Response:
{ "access_token": "...", "expires_in": 3600, "token_type": "Bearer" }

request.description:
The full workflow result — decision, risk score, and each capability's outcome (extraction, similarity, liveness, usability, dataChecks, imageChecks). Mirrors JumioClient.retrieveWorkflow in src/lib/jumio/client.ts.

No request body. Uses the tenant bearer token from Step 1, not the transaction-scoped token returned in the account-create reply — that one only authorizes uploads for its own workflow execution.

Retry policy, as implemented in src/lib/jumio/retrieval.ts: 404 / 429 / 5xx / network errors are retried at 1s, 3s, 8s, 10s. A 404 here means "not visible yet" far more often than "does not exist". A 400 or 403 is our own bad request and repeating it only spends rate limit.

decision.type is PASSED | WARNING | REJECTED | NOT_EXECUTED.
decision.risk.score is 0 (no risk) to 100; -1 means the workflow never executed.

The response also carries credentials[].parts[].href, pointing at the ID and selfie images. FreightID deliberately never fetches or stores those.
